balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Anglo American plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

copperNickelProduction.title: Copper and nickel production
copperNickelProduction.content:
Copper (thousand tonnes) is Anglo's Chile/Peru operations (Los Bronces, Collahuasi, Quellaveco); nickel is the Barro Alto ferronickel operation in Brazil.

For Anglo American plc: copper is the strategic centrepiece -- the FY2025 portfolio simplification (demerging the platinum business as Valterra Platinum, pursuing a De Beers separation) was explicitly to concentrate on copper, and in 2025 Anglo agreed a merger of equals with Teck Resources to form "Anglo Teck", a copper-focused leader built partly on Quellaveco's ramp-up. Volume here, not price, is the lever management controls quarter to quarter.

What to watch:

  • Quellaveco's ramp toward full capacity versus grade decline at the older Chilean pits
  • Progress of the Anglo Teck merger and what it does to the combined copper volume base

bulkMaterialsProduction.title: Iron ore and steelmaking coal production
bulkMaterialsProduction.content:
Iron ore (million tonnes) is almost entirely Kumba Iron Ore (South Africa) plus Minas-Rio (Brazil); steelmaking coal is the Queensland (Australia) operations.

For Anglo American plc: Anglo agreed to sell Steelmaking Coal in a November 2024 deal with Peabody Energy, but Peabody later declined to complete the purchase of the balance of the business after an underground incident and the suspension of the Grosvenor mine (the Jellinbah mine was sold separately at end-2024) -- so this volume line is now a live operational question again, not a settled divestment. Kumba is also logistics-constrained: Transnet rail and port capacity has repeatedly capped how much ore it can actually sell.

What to watch:

  • Kumba volumes against Transnet rail performance, not just the mine plan
  • Steelmaking Coal volume and the outcome of the Peabody dispute/divestment process

manganeseProduction.title: Manganese ore production
manganeseProduction.content:
Manganese ore (thousand tonnes) is produced by the Samancor joint venture (South Africa and Groote Eylandt, Australia) and sold mostly into steel alloying.

For Anglo American plc: it is a smaller, steel-cycle-linked revenue line rather than a strategic pillar, so a volume dip here matters far less to the thesis than the same move in copper.

What to watch:

  • Volume swings tracking Chinese steel demand more than company-specific execution

diamondProduction.title: Diamond production
diamondProduction.content:
Diamonds (million carats) are De Beers' output, sold through De Beers' own sales channel rather than at spot, and management actively trims output to match demand (2026 guidance is 21-26 million carats).

For Anglo American plc: De Beers is pursuing a dual-track separation -- a demerger or a structured sale process -- that was still under way and not yet classified held-for-sale as at 31 December 2025, so production here describes a business in transition, not a steady-state driver of group value.

What to watch:

  • Deliberate output cuts to match weak rough-diamond demand, which will show up as falling volume without a mine problem behind it
  • Progress and terms of the De Beers separation

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Anglo American plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Anglo American plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Anglo American plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Anglo American plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Anglo American plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Anglo American plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Anglo American plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Anglo American plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Anglo American plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
